children: Bond-market volatility is again becoming an important driver of stocks, with the relationship between the ICE BofA MOVE Index and the S&P 500
turning more negative as Treasury volatility rises, The Kobeissi Letter said in a post on X.

The 30-day correlation between the MOVE Index and the S&P 500 has fallen to -0.58, its most negative reading since mid-June. A more negative reading means bond volatility and stocks have been moving more consistently in opposite directions.

The MOVE Index, often called the “VIX of bonds,” measures yield volatility across 2-year, 5-year, 10-year and 30-year U.S. Treasuries. The Kobeissi Letter said rapid increases in bond volatility are now translating into larger declines in stock prices.
The MOVE Index has surged 8.0% over the past week to 80.7, putting it near its highest level since mid-May, according to The Kobeissi Letter.
A similar pattern occurred in March this year and in April 2025, when sharp moves in the MOVE Index exacerbated market selloffs, the letter said.
Bond volatility is again becoming a key driver of stocks, the Kobeissi Letter said.

title: Bond volatility is back in the driver’s seat for stocks
